title: domains.json
description: Shape of components/kg-content/entities/domains.json -- the single, consolidated file for the `domain` entity type, a scoped exception to kg-core's usual one-file-per-entity convention. See SCHEMA.md's `domain` section for why. No automated validator wired up yet (stdlib-only convention; skipping a jsonschema dependency rather than breaking it -- see kg-core/README.md).

schema_version.description: Marked -experimental while domain's shape is still provisional -- see SCHEMA.md.

source.description: The Confluence page this was ingested from.

owner.description: Role, never a personal name -- see CLAUDE.md's no-personal-names rule.

id.description: Permanent, kebab-case, unprefixed -- matches kg-core/SCHEMA.md's id convention for every other entity type even though domain no longer gets its own file.

category.description: Must be one of the ids listed in the top-level `categories` array. Not enforced as a JSON Schema enum here because it would duplicate `categories` and drift; check it against that array instead.

status.description: Same vocabulary as every other kg-core entity type (SCHEMA.md's frontmatter contract).

scope.description: Whether the domain exists specifically for the payment-acquiring business or serves Tyro as a whole. A judgement made in this repo, not a fact from the source page. Deliberately binary (a three-valued `both` was proposed and rejected) and consumers must dim rather than hide out-of-scope domains -- see SCHEMA.md's `scope` section and decision 35.

scope_note.description: Present only where the `scope` call is genuinely arguable, recording which way it could have gone and why. Absence means nobody has recorded a doubt yet -- not that the call is certain.

owns.description: Short capability/data-ownership phrases -- lean by design, not a transcription of the source's full capability-authority and data-authority lists.

content.description: What is specifically excluded -- the thing a solution-phase reader might otherwise assume this domain covers. Free text, sourced from the same Confluence page's own per-domain 'Explicit non-authority' bullets, not invented here.

ref.description: The domain that owns `content` instead. Must be another domain's `id` unless `unresolved` is set -- see that property.

unresolved.description: Present (and always true) only when `ref` could not be resolved to a real domain id -- e.g. a collective phrase like 'Relevant product domains' or 'All authoritative domains' that names no single domain, or a legacy source term this ingestion never split cleanly. Absence means `ref` is a real id; do not add this to soften an unresolved case into a resolved-looking one, and do not resolve a collective phrase to one id just to avoid setting it.

items.description: One explicit non-authority claim, pairing what is excluded with who owns it instead. Was a plain string, and briefly a structured `relationships[]` edge type before that (both removed -- see SCHEMA.md's Open items): this shape restores the content half that both versions dropped, without reintroducing a graph edge -- `ref` is not required to resolve to an id that itself points back, and nothing renders this as a graph.

not_authoritative_for.description: Every non-authority claim this domain's source page makes, each paired with the specific content excluded -- see the item schema.
